# The profinite integers are topologically generated by one

This module proves the theorem
`Langlands.NYLL.ClassFormation.zHatOne_topologicallyGenerates`.
Its type is exactly the already published proposition
`Langlands.NYLL.ClassFormation.zHatOne_topologicallyGeneratesStatement`
from [`../Statements.lean`](../Statements.lean).
This is the proof phase of M008.024 in the
[NYLL partition](../../../../../../notes/reuse/nyll-public-port/m001-m024.md#m008).

## Target

The target has no parameters and no universe parameter. It unfolds to

```lean
TopologicallyGenerates
  (G := Multiplicative ZHat)
  ({Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ZHat)} : Set (Multiplicative ZHat))
```

Here `ZHat : Type 0` is the published NYLL closure model from
`Langlands.NYLL.GaloisCohomology.ProfiniteIntegers.ProfiniteIntegerCore.Definitions`:
the topological closure of the diagonal image of `ℤ` in the product
`∀ i : PortInternal.M008.d001, ZMod i.modulus` over all positive moduli,
with its subspace topology and its commutative ring structure.
`Multiplicative ZHat` is its additive group written multiplicatively, so its
group operation is addition in `ZHat`, with Mathlib's transported topology
and topological-group structure. `TopologicallyGenerates X` is the published
NYLL definition `(Subgroup.closure X).topologicalClosure = ⊤`. So the
conclusion says that the closure of the abstract subgroup generated by
`ofAdd 1`, i.e. of the integer multiples of `1`, is all of `ZHat`.

## Implemented proof

The proof first unfolds the published proposition with `show` to the
expression above, and then follows the original proof at lines 204–224
without changing its steps.

1. Let `f : Multiplicative ℤ →* Multiplicative ZHat` be
   `AddMonoidHom.toMultiplicative (Int.castRingHom ZHat).toAddMonoidHom`
   (`Mathlib/Algebra/Group/TypeTags/Hom.lean`, line 25), so
   `f = ofAdd ∘ Int.cast ∘ toAdd`.
2. `hf : DenseRange f`. The maps `Multiplicative.ofAdd : ZHat → Multiplicative ZHat`
   and `Multiplicative.toAdd : Multiplicative ℤ → ℤ` are surjective, hence
   have dense range by `Function.Surjective.denseRange`
   (`Mathlib/Topology/Continuous.lean`, line 265). The published density
   theorem `denseRange_intCast_zHat` (M008.023) gives that the integer cast
   `ℤ → ZHat` has dense range. Two applications of `DenseRange.comp`
   (`Mathlib/Topology/Continuous.lean`, line 309) compose these: first with
   continuity of `ofAdd` (`continuous_id`, line 108 of the same file, since
   the topology on `Multiplicative ZHat` is that of `ZHat`), then with
   continuity of the cast, which holds by `continuous_of_discreteTopology`
   (`Mathlib/Topology/Order.lean`, line 334) because `ℤ` is discrete.
   `simpa [f, Function.comp_def]` identifies the composite with `f`.
3. The published M007.008 theorem
   `topologicallyGenerates_singleton_of_denseRange_mint`, applied to `f` and
   `hf`, gives `TopologicallyGenerates {f (ofAdd 1)}`. `simpa [f]`
   rewrites `f (ofAdd 1)` to `ofAdd (1 : ZHat)` (via the cast of `1`),
   which is the goal.

The proof uses only these two published theorems, the imported definitions
and Mathlib. A development check compiled the module with no errors or
warnings; the theorem has no level parameter and its axioms are only
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. This check does not
establish independent semantic acceptance or publication.
